newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore economy grew 6.5 pct in 1996 - PM.
newsitem.headline: Singapore economy grew 6.5 pct in 1996 - PM.

text.p: The Singapore economy grew by 6.5 percent in 1996 and is expected to make steady growth of between five and seven percent in 1997, Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said in a statement on Tuesday.
He also said inflation for 1996 remained low at 1.3 percent while wages grew by 6.1 percent.
The prime minister, in his new year message to Singaporeans, said the economy slowed down in the second half of 1996 because of the global electronics downturn and other cyclical factors.
But he noted the flow of inward investment remains strong. Manufacturing investment commitments reached a record Singapore $8.1 billion in 1996.
"We should have no difficulty making steady growth of 5-7 percent in 1997," Goh said.
Last month the government had forecast economic growth for 1996 at around six percent.
